function: Spectrum pricing for LEO satellite spectrum leasing, learned by federated DDQN to maximize revenue; the action is only the price level (p. 7, Eq. 11).
notes: above_phy. The learned element is a DDQN per satellite, aggregated by blockchain-driven FL, and it sets the price of leased spectrum to maximize revenue. p. 7: "δs denotes the price level decision" (the state is price and utility, Eq. 10, and the reward is the utility change, Eq. 12). p. 1: "to learn a revenue-maximizing pricing scheme". Spectrum pricing is a market and network-management decision above the PHY. Power control is credited to the non-learned reputation mechanism. p. 1: "reputation-based blockchain which is used in the global model aggregation phase of FL to optimize the power control". The power level also works as an access threshold. p. 6: "if the required transmit power of a terrestrial user is bigger than the power control of the LEO satellite, then that user will not select this satellite's spectrum to lease". Results report only reward, price, and revenue (Section V, Figs. 7-10, pp. 11-14). For the reviewer: Algorithm 1 (p. 7) lets the action "change the price of the spectrum or the control level of power", and p. 8 says the DDQN searches "the optimal spectrum price and power control". But the MDP defines no power action (Eq. 11), and no power result is reported. If the reviewer reads this as learned satellite power control, the work passes to area 6, where it would have a custom channel without TR 38.811, separate training per setting, Fig. 10 baselines (average-budget price, and DDQN without FL, p. 14), complexity on p. 10, and no code. FL aggregates digitally among terrestrial servers (p. 9), not over the air, so it is not area 7. The PDF is arXiv:2407.00814v2 (12 Jun 2025). Its title and authors match the Crossref record of the DOI.
